Dangerous goods compliance and training

We help transport, warehousing and manufacturing operators meet dangerous goods legislation without slowing their operations down. Our consultants audit your current practice, identify the gaps against the regulations that apply to your cargo, and give you a written remediation plan your team can act on. We then train the people who handle that cargo so the plan survives staff turnover.

Consulting and auditing

An audit covers documentation, packaging, labelling, placarding, vehicle equipment and driver competence. We review your consignment paperwork against the classification of the goods you actually move, inspect a representative sample of vehicles, and interview the staff responsible for loading. You receive a findings register ranked by risk, with the regulation each finding relates to and a practical correction for each one. Most operators close the majority of findings within a single quarter once the register exists.

Accredited training

Training runs at our centre or on your site. Courses cover classification, packing, marking and labelling, documentation, loading and segregation, and emergency response. Every delegate is assessed and certificated, and we keep a register so you can prove competence at a roadside inspection or a customer audit. We also run refresher sessions timed to the renewal cycle so nobody on your team lapses without warning.

Signage, equipment and documentation

We supply the placards, labels, emergency information panels, spill kits and trem cards your fleet needs, matched to the classes you carry. Ordering the right item for the right class is where most operators lose time, so we specify it from your own consignment data rather than a generic catalogue.

What a typical engagement looks like

A first assessment takes one day for a small fleet and up to a week for a multi-site operation. The written report follows within ten working days, and training can usually be scheduled in the same month.
